parameters.cooling_method: casting into ceramic molds heated to 900°C

evidence.quote: The modification of the structure and phase state of the alloy was carried out by introducing the composite powders into the melt at a temperature of 1480–1500°C and, after 1.5–2-min holding, casting the melt into ceramic mold s heated to a temperature of 900°C d i r e c t l y i n t h e v a c u u m c h a m b e r o f a n induction furnace.

process_steps.input_state: nickel and aluminum powder mixtures with nanosized TiN powder

evidence.quote: NiAl-based composite compacts were prepared via the high-temperature synthesis of an intermetallic compound under pressure in nickel and aluminum powder mixtures with a stoichiometric composition, which comprised the predetermined amount of the nanosized powders of the refractory compounds.
The synthesized composite compacts were mechanically ground to obtain composite powder particles with a specified size.

In the first case, the refractory nanoparticles exhibit a nucleating effect on the grain structure formation of the alloy (an increase in the number of the crystallization nuclei in the melt).
In the second case, the refractory nanoparticles stop the movement of grain boundaries during the formation of the grain structure of the alloy .

The precipitation of the nanoparticles of refractory compounds at the boundaries of the formed grains slow down the recrystallization processes, i.e., it prevents the growth of grains that are in contact with each other.
